key_inputs: Registered voters 7,331,981 (CEC figure reported 26 Oct 2026); 2022 turnout was 70.6% of 6,788,804. About 810,000 eligibles live abroad (CBS via Walla, 21 Oct) and almost none can vote, so the headline rate sits under 2022 even with high in-country motivation.

Believed Friday cluster, not the average with Channel 14: Midgam/Channel 12 (n=1018, 23 Oct) coalition 50, Yashar 23, Likud 21, Together 15, Reservists 2.4%, Amcha 2.5%; Kantar/Kan 11 (n=1006) coalition 50 with Reservists at 4 seats and Amcha 2.9%; Madad/Channel 13 (n=1875) coalition 50, Amcha 3.1%, Reservists 3.0%; Maariv/Lazar coalition 48; Israel Hayom/Kantar coalition 50. i24/Direct Polls Likud 26 and a 55-seat coalition on this bloc definition; Channel 14/Next Data (Filber, n=7937, 22 Oct) Likud 30 and coalition 62.

House effects and records: Direct Polls/i24 about +5 to +8 coalition seats vs the pack this year, Next Data/Channel 14 about +8, and both are online panels with no phone. In 2022 final polls the coalition averaged about 60 and won 64; Direct Polls' final was 62, Midgam and Kantar 60. That is a two-seat edge, not a twelve-seat one. April 2019 and 2015 Likud late swings were real but mostly consolidation inside the right, not a bloc-sized miss. Shas beat 2022 polls by about 3 seats; this year's stated Haredi turnout is lower (Hasid: about 75% willing vs 82% actual in 2022), so no Shas add-on.

Threshold and withdrawals: Reservists and Amcha left below 3.25% because the last Channel 12 and 13 polls put them there and Israeli lists polling 2.5-3.2% usually fail (Zehut and New Right 2019, Meretz and Balad 2022). Their wasted votes are already inside the 50-seat polls, so the 2022 +4 bloc correction is not applied again. Blue and White and Ahi resigned and are off the 36-list ballot; Ahi endorsed Likud from a sub-1% base. Surplus pairs used: Likud+RZP-Zehut, Shas+UTJ, Together+Yisrael Beiteinu, Yashar+Democrats, Joint List+Ra'am.

What moved the point forecast versus Channel 12: Likud 21 to 22 and Democrats 10 to 9. The Likud seat is the weekend gevalt (Trump endorsement, Netanyahu's 26 Oct appeal to Zelekha voters, Western Wall pitch) plus a small double-envelope tilt to young right voters. Arab turnout intention up (Stat-Net 63% vs about 53-56% in 2022; Hasid about 65%) keeps Joint List+Ra'am at 14 rather than a collapse. Social signals added that one Likud seat and reinforced the two threshold failures; they did not justify Channel 14.

notes: The forecast follows Friday's Midgam, Kantar, Madad and Lazar cluster (coalition 48-52) and treats Channel 14 and i24 as an 8-12 seat right-panel house effect, not as half the average; Direct Polls was only about two seats closer than the pack in 2022, not twelve. A one-seat Likud lift versus the Channel 12 poll reflects the late race for first, Trump's endorsement and Netanyahu's 26 October pitch to Zelekha's voters, while lower stated Haredi turnout and higher stated Arab turnout offset the old Shas undercount. Reservists (2.7%) and Amcha (2.4%) are projected to miss 3.25%, as lists in that band usually do; Blue and White and Ahi are off the ballot, and the micro-lists (Noam, Black Color, Israel First and the rest) sit in other. Social media showed intense Likud base mobilization but the same kind of online noise that overstated Zehut in 2019, so it moved the totals by about one seat and did not put the coalition on 61. Yashar remains the largest list and the blocs land at 51, 55 and 14.
